raw: 20.1 The Psychology of Influence: Cialdini's Seven Principles[^97]
teaching_note: The seven-item formulation is edition-dependent: the author's 2021 edition announcement identifies unity as new, establishing list identity but not independent efficacy (https://www.influenceatwork.com/announcement/the-new-revision-of-influence/); the inherited vendor history does not establish that edition or universal effects. As defensive recognition prompts: reciprocity → obligation is not authorization; commitment/consistency → recheck a changed request; social proof → popularity is not authenticity; liking → familiarity is not identity; authority → verify role independently; scarcity → urgency does not remove checks; unity → shared identity does not confer access. These are questions to ask, not deterministic weaknesses or persuasion instructions.
title: Influence principles: edition-bounded recognition, not vulnerability diagnosis

teaching_note: Treat a security vendor's historical overview as practitioner context with selection and commercial incentives, not a complete history or controlled evaluation. Separate recurring request patterns from changing communication channels; an anecdote cannot establish incidence, effectiveness or a person's susceptibility [@ageint097].
title: History of Social Engineering

raw: 20.3 Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking (Hadnagy, 2018)[^98]
teaching_note: The book's title is not a scientific-validity finding: classify its assertions as practitioner advice, anecdote or supported study before relying on them. Extract defensive recognition and verification questions only; no elicitation scripts, deceptive practice on classmates or tests of personal vulnerability [@ageint098].
title: Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking (Hadnagy, 2018)

teaching_note: Compare the two practitioner editions by the problem and evidence they describe, not by treating repeated examples as independent replications. A convincing story about rapport or authority does not establish an individual's motive, diagnosis or propensity to comply [@ageint099].
title: The Art of Human Hacking (Hadnagy, 2010)

raw: 20.5 Phishing, Vishing, Smishing, Deepfake Voice Attacks
teaching_note: Email, voice and text differ as channels, but the defensive question is whether the request and requester are independently authenticated; perceived voice realism is not identity proof. Completed offline case: Q1 is an urgent synthetic voice transcript requesting a roster; Q2 is a text claiming the same authority; Q3 is a previously supplied directory card with the approved verification route. The worked answer pauses disclosure, uses Q3 rather than contact details inside Q1/Q2, and records only request type and verification status; agreement between two messages does not authenticate either. Withheld Q4 shows an authorized scheduling error, so revise from 'possible impersonation' to 'misrouted legitimate request', correct the record without blame and stop; the packet never establishes theft, AI generation or a real person's intent.
title: Phishing, Vishing, Smishing, Deepfake Voice Attacks

raw: 20.6 Physical Social Engineering: Access, Elicitation, Impersonation
teaching_note: An unfamiliar visitor, unusual question or apparent role mismatch is not guilt; disability, unfamiliar procedures and honest mistakes are credible alternatives. Teach courteous referral to an authorized access/help process and protection of private information, not surveillance, confrontation, impersonation or covert questioning; the broad cited guidance does not validate particular physical techniques.
title: Physical Social Engineering: Access, Elicitation, Impersonation

raw: 20.7 AI Automation of Social Engineering at Scale[^100]
teaching_note: A survey's reports of agent capabilities inherit each underlying study's task, permissions and evaluation conditions; they are not deployed success rates for all adversaries. Distinguish generated content, attempted contact, authenticated access and actual harm, and do not infer automation from fluent or repetitive language alone [@ageint100].
title: AI Automation of Social Engineering at Scale

teaching_note: Training recognition, independent verification and access controls address different failure paths; none is a guarantee or proof that users are to blame when systems fail. Any proposed classroom simulation is disclosed, consensual, non-punitive and debriefed, with no live messages, credentials or personal scoring. A correct synthetic answer demonstrates reasoning within the packet, not durable behavior change or real-world efficacy.
title: Defense: Training, Simulation, Technical Controls
